jordan/amman-citadel.name: Amman Citadel
jordan/amman-citadel.description: A hilltop archaeological site above downtown Amman with the Temple of Hercules and the Umayyad Palace.
jordan/amman-citadel.details: The Citadel crowns one of the hills of Amman and holds remains from the Roman, Byzantine and Umayyad periods, including the columns of the Temple of Hercules and the Umayyad Palace complex. The small Jordan Archaeological Museum is on site. It gives wide views over the city and is best in late afternoon, when the light is soft and the heat eases. Wear sturdy shoes; paths are uneven.

jordan/roman-theatre-amman.name: Roman Theatre and downtown Amman
jordan/roman-theatre-amman.description: A restored second-century Roman theatre in the middle of the old downtown, with souks and cafes around it.
jordan/roman-theatre-amman.details: The Roman Theatre seats about six thousand and sits at the heart of downtown Amman, a short walk from lively streets of spice sellers, sweet shops and falafel stands. Two small museums are tucked into the sides of the theatre. The climb to the top row is steep. Downtown is busiest in the evening, and Friday mornings are quiet because shops close.

jordan/rainbow-street.name: Rainbow Street
jordan/rainbow-street.description: A lively Amman street of cafes, bookshops and rooftop terraces popular for an evening stroll.
jordan/rainbow-street.details: Rainbow Street runs through the Jabal Amman district and is the place locals and visitors head to for coffee, snacks and sunset from a rooftop terrace. Side streets hold craft shops and small galleries. It is most lively on weekend evenings. Prices vary widely from street food to full restaurant meals.

jordan/jerash.name: Jerash
jordan/jerash.description: One of the best-preserved Roman provincial cities in the world, with colonnaded streets, temples and theatres.
jordan/jerash.details: Jerash, ancient Gerasa, has a long colonnaded street, an oval plaza, two theatres and the Temple of Artemis, all in remarkable condition. It lies about an hour north of Amman. Go early to beat the heat and the tour groups; there is almost no shade. A hippodrome show with chariot races and legionary drills runs on a set schedule.

jordan/ajloun-castle.name: Ajloun Castle
jordan/ajloun-castle.description: A twelfth-century hilltop fortress in pine-covered hills north of Jerash, built to guard against crusaders.
jordan/ajloun-castle.details: Ajloun Castle was built in 1184 by an Ayyubid commander and commands views across the Jordan Valley. Inside are vaulted halls and a small museum. The surrounding hills are green, with pine and oak forest that feels very different from the desert south. It is often combined with Jerash on a day trip from Amman.

jordan/umm-qais.name: Umm Qais
jordan/umm-qais.description: A hilltop ruin of ancient Gadara with basalt theatre seats and views over the Sea of Galilee and the Golan Heights.
jordan/umm-qais.details: Umm Qais is the site of the Decapolis city of Gadara, with black basalt columns and a theatre built of dark stone. Its main attraction is the view, across the Yarmouk valley to the Sea of Galilee and the Golan Heights. It is quiet compared with Jerash. It sits close to a border area, so carry your passport.

jordan/madaba-mosaics.name: Madaba mosaics
jordan/madaba-mosaics.description: A town known for its Byzantine mosaics, including a sixth-century map of the Holy Land in St George's Church.
jordan/madaba-mosaics.details: Madaba is called the City of Mosaics. The Greek Orthodox Church of St George holds a sixth-century mosaic map of the Holy Land made of about two million pieces. The Archaeological Park and the Church of the Apostles have more floors. The town is small, friendly and easy to explore on foot. Dress modestly in churches.

jordan/mount-nebo.name: Mount Nebo
jordan/mount-nebo.description: The mountain from which Moses is said to have seen the Promised Land, with a memorial church and sweeping valley views.
jordan/mount-nebo.details: Mount Nebo rises above the Jordan Valley and the Dead Sea. A Byzantine church on the summit shelters fine mosaics, and a serpent sculpture marks the viewing platform. On a clear day Jerusalem and Jericho can be seen in the distance. It is a short stop, usually combined with Madaba.

jordan/bethany-baptism-site.name: Bethany Beyond the Jordan
jordan/bethany-baptism-site.description: The traditional site of Jesus's baptism, with ruined churches and baptism pools by the Jordan River.
jordan/bethany-baptism-site.details: This UNESCO site on the east bank of the Jordan River is reached on a guided walk from the visitor centre, past ruined Byzantine churches and baptism pools. The river here is narrow and slow. It is hot in summer, so go in the morning. A guide is required, and the visit takes around two hours.

jordan/kerak-castle.name: Kerak Castle
jordan/kerak-castle.description: A large crusader fortress on the King's Highway, with long vaulted passages, towers and valley views.
jordan/kerak-castle.details: Kerak Castle was built by the crusaders in the twelfth century and later extended by the Mamluks. Long dark vaulted galleries run through the walls and can be explored with a torch. It sits on the old King's Highway between Madaba and Petra, so many routes stop here. Wear shoes with good grip.

jordan/desert-castles.name: Desert castles and Qusayr Amra
jordan/desert-castles.description: Eighth-century Umayyad desert retreats east of Amman, including Qusayr Amra with its painted bathhouse frescoes.
jordan/desert-castles.details: The Umayyad rulers built hunting lodges and bathhouses in the eastern desert, including Qusayr Amra, a UNESCO site with rare wall paintings of hunting and bathing scenes, and the fortress of Qasr Kharana. They are best reached by car or on a tour in half a day from Amman. There is little shade and no services, so bring water.

jordan/petra-treasury.name: Petra: Siq and the Treasury
jordan/petra-treasury.description: The narrow canyon entrance to Petra, ending at the famous rose-red Treasury carved into the cliff.
jordan/petra-treasury.details: The walk to the Treasury starts at the visitor centre and follows the Siq, a winding canyon about 1.2 kilometres long with high walls, to the Treasury (Al-Khazneh). Early morning, before the groups arrive, is best for light and quiet. The whole site is much bigger than most expect, so allow a full day with comfortable shoes and plenty of water. Horses, carts and camels are available, and the way back is uphill.

jordan/petra-monastery.name: Petra: the Monastery
jordan/petra-monastery.description: A hike of around 850 rock-cut steps to a huge carved monument high above the main valley.
jordan/petra-monastery.details: The Monastery (Ad-Deir) is even larger than the Treasury but much quieter. The climb is about 800 steps from the valley floor, taking an hour or more, and is steep in places. Donkeys are offered but not recommended for welfare reasons. Start in the cooler morning and carry water. Views from the cliff edge beyond the Monastery are spectacular.

jordan/petra-by-night.name: Petra by Night
jordan/petra-by-night.description: An evening walk through the Siq lit by candles to the Treasury, with music and tea.
jordan/petra-by-night.details: Petra by Night is held on certain evenings of the week (usually Monday, Wednesday and Thursday), when around 1,500 candles light the Siq and the Treasury square. Visitors sit on mats for a short performance of music and storytelling with tea. Tickets are bought separately at the visitor centre. It lasts about two hours and is atmospheric rather than a place for photographs.

jordan/little-petra.name: Little Petra
jordan/little-petra.description: A smaller Nabataean site just north of Petra with a short siq, carved rooms and a painted ceiling.
jordan/little-petra.details: Siq al-Barid, or Little Petra, was a suburb of the Nabataean capital with carved dining rooms and homes along a short canyon. It is free of crowds and quick to explore. The Painted House has traces of colourful frescoes. It is often visited at dusk or before Petra, and a scramble up its stairs gives views over the valley.

jordan/wadi-rum-jeep.name: Wadi Rum jeep tour
jordan/wadi-rum-jeep.description: A guided drive with a Bedouin driver across red sand and past sandstone arches and canyons.
jordan/wadi-rum-jeep.details: Wadi Rum, the Valley of the Moon, is a protected desert of red sand and towering sandstone cliffs. Local Bedouin guides drive visitors in 4x4 trucks to sites such as Khazali Canyon, the Burdah rock bridge and sand dunes, with tea stops. Tours run from two hours to a full day. Sun protection and a scarf help with the glare and dust.

jordan/wadi-rum-sunset-camp.name: Wadi Rum sunset and desert camp
jordan/wadi-rum-sunset-camp.description: A sunset on the dunes followed by a Bedouin dinner cooked underground and a night of stars.
jordan/wadi-rum-sunset-camp.details: After the day tour, visitors watch the sun set over the cliffs, then return to a desert camp for zarb, a traditional meal of meat and vegetables cooked in a pit in the sand. The sky is exceptionally dark, giving a brilliant view of the stars. Nights are cold in winter, so bring warm layers.

jordan/wadi-rum-camel.name: Camel ride in Wadi Rum
jordan/wadi-rum-camel.description: A short ride across the desert with a Bedouin guide, usually near sunset or sunrise.
jordan/wadi-rum-camel.details: Camel rides in Wadi Rum range from one hour to a full day and are offered by Bedouin families. Sunset is the most popular time. The ride is slow and gentle, though getting on and off can be a jolt. Check the animals look healthy and are well treated before booking.

jordan/aqaba-snorkel.name: Red Sea snorkelling in Aqaba
jordan/aqaba-snorkel.description: Snorkelling or a boat trip over coral reefs and a wreck in the Gulf of Aqaba.
jordan/aqaba-snorkel.details: Aqaba is Jordan's only coastal city, with warm water and good reefs just offshore. Boat trips include snorkel stops, and the Cedar Pride wreck is a popular dive site. Equipment is cheap to hire. The gulf is quiet and calm, a relaxing end to a desert trip. The city is hot in summer, so book morning sessions.

jordan/dead-sea-float.name: Floating in the Dead Sea
jordan/dead-sea-float.description: A float in water so salty that nobody sinks, at the lowest point on land, with mud treatments on the shore.
jordan/dead-sea-float.details: The Dead Sea lies about 430 metres below sea level. Its water is around ten times as salty as the ocean, so bathers float without effort. Smearing black mud on the skin is the traditional treatment. Do not shave beforehand, avoid getting water in the eyes, and rinse in the fresh-water showers afterwards. Resort day passes are available for non-guests.

jordan/wadi-mujib.name: Wadi Mujib canyon
jordan/wadi-mujib.description: A water-filled canyon where visitors wade, scramble and swim through a narrow gorge to a waterfall.
jordan/wadi-mujib.details: The Siq Trail at Wadi Mujib follows a stream through a narrow canyon, wading and swimming to a waterfall. Lifejackets are provided and the guides help with ropes. The trail is only open from about April to October, as flash floods are a risk in the wet season. Wear water shoes and expect to be soaked.

jordan/dana-reserve.name: Dana Biosphere Reserve
jordan/dana-reserve.description: Jordan's largest nature reserve, with hiking trails between an old stone village and the desert of Wadi Araba.
jordan/dana-reserve.details: Dana Biosphere Reserve covers mountains, valleys and desert, and holds several habitats in a short distance. Guided or self-guided trails descend from the old stone village of Dana. Wildlife includes ibex and many birds. The village is quiet, with views over Wadi Dana, and it is a good place to end a day. Spring and autumn are the best seasons.

jordan.description: A desert kingdom of Petra, Wadi Rum, Roman ruins and the Dead Sea, with warm hospitality.

jordan/amman.name: Amman
jordan/amman.description: Jordan's hilly capital, with a Roman theatre, a hilltop citadel and a lively cafe and food scene.

jordan/jerash.name: Jerash
jordan/jerash.description: A town north of Amman beside one of the best-preserved Roman cities in the Middle East.

jordan/madaba.name: Madaba
jordan/madaba.description: A small town of Byzantine mosaics, close to Mount Nebo and the Dead Sea.

jordan/dana.name: Dana
jordan/dana.description: A stone village on the edge of Dana Biosphere Reserve, with hiking trails and desert views.

jordan/petra.name: Petra
jordan/petra.description: The rose-red Nabataean capital carved into the cliffs, reached from the town of Wadi Musa.

jordan/wadi-rum.name: Wadi Rum
jordan/wadi-rum.description: A protected desert of red sand and sandstone cliffs, explored with Bedouin guides and camps.

jordan/aqaba.name: Aqaba
jordan/aqaba.description: Jordan's Red Sea port, with warm water, coral reefs and a relaxed seaside feel.

jordan/dead-sea.name: Dead Sea
jordan/dead-sea.description: The lowest point on land, with salty water that lets bathers float.

jordan/ma-an.name: Ma'an Governorate
jordan/ma-an.description: The southern governorate that includes Petra, the Dana area and the desert highlands.
